decision_description: In the Phase 7 budget gate assessment for run 9e27694f-e13b-4449-9436-93623b7873bf (instrument MSCA-PF, unit-cost regime), a conflict arose between two authorities. The conflicting authorities are: (1) the budget-gate skill specification under .claude/skills/ (authority hierarchy priority 9), whose lump-sum-oriented Mode B check requires a validated external Lump Sum Budget Planner response in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ and treats an empty received/ directory as a blocking Phase 7 gate failure; and (2) the constitution CLAUDE.md (authority hierarchy priority 2), whose §8.1/§8.4 as amended by C1 make the budget gate instrument-conditional by source and sanction an internal deterministic unit-cost derivation (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json) as the budget source for unit-cost instruments, scoping the 'exclusively external' received/ requirement to lump-sum instruments only. The specific issue in conflict is whether the empty lump-sum received/ directory constitutes a blocking Phase 7 gate failure for this unit-cost MSCA-PF instrument. Resolution: the constitution prevails over the skill specification; the lump-sum Mode B received/-directory check does not fire as a blocking failure for a unit-cost instrument, and gate_09 passes on the complete, all-Confirmed deterministic derivation (unresolved_components empty, blocking_inconsistencies empty).
alternatives_considered: Treat the empty docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ directory as a blocking Phase 7 gate failure per the skill specification's lump-sum Mode B check — rejected because CLAUDE.md governs over .claude/skills/ per §3 and amendment C1 scopes the external-response requirement to lump-sum instruments only, not to this unit-cost MSCA-PF instrument.

Hold the gate in a pending/wait state until an external lump-sum response is received — rejected because §8.4 as amended by C1 makes the absence of a lump-sum external response a blocking failure (not a hold) for lump-sum instruments only, and for unit-cost instruments the sanctioned source is the internal deterministic derivation, which is present and complete.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §3 (authority hierarchy: CLAUDE.md at priority 2 governs over .claude/skills/ at priority 9, resolving the conflict in favour of the constitution); CLAUDE.md §8.1 and §8.4 as amended by C1 (for unit-cost instruments the internal deterministic derivation is the sole sanctioned budget source and the 'exclusively external' received/ requirement is scoped to lump-sum instruments only); CLAUDE.md §15 and §10.2 (the constitution governs over any conflicting skill specification, and a skill is an execution aid, not an authority).
rationale: The constitution is the highest interpretive authority below an explicit in-session human override (§2, §15), and §3 explicitly ranks CLAUDE.md above .claude/skills/. Amendment C1 makes the budget gate instrument-conditional by source: for unit-cost instruments (MSCA-PF) the anti-fabrication guarantee is supplied by deterministic, byte-equal-checked derivation from published unit costs rather than by externalisation, so the lump-sum received/ requirement does not apply. Applying the skill's lump-sum Mode B check as a blocking failure here would import a lump-sum-only precondition into a unit-cost instrument, contradicting §8.4's instrument-independence and §2's programme-agnostic mission. The categorical Phase-8 block (§8.4, §13.4) is preserved rather than weakened: gate_09 passes only because every budget component in unit_cost_budget.json resolves to Confirmed with unresolved_components and blocking_inconsistencies both empty, and the derivation is closed by a byte-equal replay check. Resolving the conflict the other way would have been the constitutionally prohibited act of allowing a lower-priority skill specification to override a higher-priority constitutional rule.
